evidence: run_sql.py:84-85 reads row_cap_hit from df.attrs[TRUNCATED_ATTR] and cap_size from df.attrs[MAX_ROWS_ATTR]; line 147 sets data=row_cap_marker_data(cap_size) if row_cap_hit else {} on the DataFrameComponent. RowCapRunner.run_sql (safety/limits.py:84-103) computes cap = effective_row_cap(self._max_rows), the min of the constructor cap and the per-request effective max_rows (limits.py:36-52), and stamps max_rows=cap, or the inner runner's already-stamped max_rows, on the df. So cap_size is the cap in effect for that query, not a fixed 10000. markers.py:56-58 builds {row_cap: int(cap)}.

RichComponent declares `data: Dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)` (core/rich_component.py:78). DataFrameComponent.__init__ forwards **kwargs to super (dataframe.py:48) and from_records merges extra kwargs into component_data (dataframe.py:~88), so `data=` is accepted and stored as a dict. row_cap_of (markers.py:61-73) reads getattr(rich,'data') dict and key 'row_cap'. The only producer of DataFrameComponent in src is run_sql.py:143-148, which passes data=row_cap_marker_data(cap) or {}; no other code sets a 'row_cap' key in data (grep of "row_cap" shows only markers, _table_payload, _format consumers and run_sql).

markers.py:61-73 row_cap_of returns None if data is not a dict (67-69), None if cap is bool, not int, or <=0 (71-72), else returns cap. Tests at tests/unit/test_run_sql_display_line.py:144-154 cover this.

In src/sqllens/_table_payload.py, _compute_table_payload sets payload['row_cap'] at lines 180-182 when row_cap_of(rich) is not None. That is before the first _serialized_len check (line 184) and before the header-only check (192) and the binary search (196-209). Every measurement therefore includes row_cap. The search loop keeps the largest mid whose serialized length is <= _MAX_TABLE_PAYLOAD_BYTES, and lo=0 was already verified by the header-only check. So the returned payload, row_cap included, is at or under the cap.

run_sql_display_line (src/sqllens/_table_payload.py:227-260) calls _compute_table_payload(rich) (line 242) and reports payload['row_count'] as N (line 251). The formatter (src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:327 -> _build_table_payload at 829-836) calls the same _compute_table_payload(rich) on the DATAFRAME component and emits {'type':'table', **payload}, so the block row_count is the same value. run_sql.py:143-152 builds the DataFrameComponent and passes that same object to run_sql_display_line and into the UiComponent. _trim_blocks_to_budget only drops whole trailing blocks and does not rewrite row_count.

src/sqllens/_table_payload.py:236-260: the whole body of run_sql_display_line (is_introspection_query, _columns_and_rows, _compute_table_payload) sits inside try/except Exception, which logs logger.warning(exc_info=True) and returns "". This covers a RuntimeError, not just ParseError. The caller at src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py:150 uses the return value with no further handling, so an exception cannot escape and the query still succeeds. Only BaseException subclasses (KeyboardInterrupt, etc.) are not caught, which is outside the claim. I did not run the monkeypatch scenario, because test suites are not run.

row_cap is set only when row_cap_of(rich) is not None (_table_payload.py:180-182); the marker is attached only when row_cap_hit (run_sql.py:147) and row_cap_of accepts only positive non-bool ints (markers.py:61-73). Field is set before first measurement (line 179-184), so it counts in the budget. Over budget, the binary search sets row_count=mid and truncated=total-mid and finalizes row_count=lo, truncated=total-lo (lines 196-213), so row_count+truncated==total and row_count==rows returned. Each candidate is measured with _serialized_len of the payload (no 'type' key) <= _MAX_TABLE_PAYLOAD_BYTES; header-only over budget returns None. Test test_both_limits_put_display_sentence_first (test_format.py:2090-2099) asserts row_cap==300, n+k and the sentence, and _serialized_len(inner without 'type') <= _MAX_TABLE_PAYLOAD_BYTES. test_uncut_table_has_no_note_and_no_row_cap_field (2102) covers absence.
